findings.checklist_item: Restate AC 1 to require sandboxing EVERY child subprocess in execute_shard() that runs shard code — explicitly the `mutmut run` mutant test-run (mutation_gate.py line 583), not only the baseline `clean` pytest at line 579 — since the destructive test executes against the mutated tree under `mutmut run`.
evidence: scripts/mutation_gate.py execute_shard() runs _run() four times: clean pytest (line 579), `mutmut run` (line 583), `mutmut results` (line 595), `mutmut show` (line 612)
The incident is described as 'a test exec'd that script' during a mutation run — the mutated-code test execution is driven by `mutmut run`, not the clean baseline at line 579
AC 1 uses the singular 'its pytest subprocess'; a `mutmut run` invocation is not literally a pytest subprocess, so the wording does not clearly require sandboxing the mutant test-run
findings.finding: AC 1 scopes the sandbox to 'its pytest subprocess' (singular), but execute_shard() spawns four subprocesses and the incident's destructive test-exec occurs during the mutant test-run driven by the `mutmut run` subprocess, not the 'clean' baseline pytest subprocess — so a literal reading of AC 1 could sandbox only the baseline and leave the causal path unsandboxed.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC 1 ('execute_shard() runs its pytest subprocess inside an OS-enforced sandbox'); Summary ('execute_shard() (line 563) runs pytest as a subprocess')
scenarios: Implementer wraps only the line-579 `clean` pytest call in the sandbox; a mutation that removes a guard is exercised under the unsandboxed `mutmut run` at line 583 and the destructive syscall lands exactly as on 2026-08-26
findings.suggested_fix: Change AC 1 to: 'execute_shard() runs each shard-executing subprocess — the baseline pytest AND the `mutmut run` mutant test-run (and any subprocess that executes shard test code) — inside the OS-enforced sandbox…'. Add an enforcement test that trips the deny under `mutmut run`, not just the clean baseline.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py as a consumer of execute_shard() and state how its source-level subprocess-argv assertion (mutmut_run_concurrency, line 948) and boundary monkeypatches are updated for the sandbox wrapper and injected HOME.
evidence: scripts/mutation_gate.py:563 execute_shard is the changed artifact; callers at lines 697-698
tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py:948 `"main": mutmut_run_concurrency("execute_shard")` asserts the exact subprocess argv structure derived from execute_shard's source
tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py:489,540 monkeypatch.setattr(gate, "execute_shard", ...)
Plan Testing lists only tests/unit/test_mutation_sandbox.py and tests/unit/test_check_destructive_test_exec.py; tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py is unmentioned
findings.finding: The plan modifies execute_shard() (sandbox-wrap its pytest/mutmut subprocess per AC 1 and inject a non-existent HOME per AC 8) but does not enumerate the existing consumer tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py, which asserts on execute_shard's own source-level subprocess call structure (line 948: mutmut_run_concurrency('execute_shard') expecting exactly ((('--max-children','1'),),)) and monkeypatches execute_shard in its flow tests.
scenarios: Wrapping pytest/mutmut in a sandbox-exec wrapper changes the argv the concurrency assertion inspects
Injecting HOME=<nonexistent> alters the child env the existing test may snapshot
findings.suggested_fix: Add tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py to Testing/DoD, noting that the mutmut_run_concurrency argv assertion must be updated to account for the sandbox wrapper prefix and that the HOME-injection assertion is added there or in the new sandbox test.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the DoD's AC cross-references so 'enforcement test' names the deny/enforcement AC (AC5) and 'fail correctly when disabled' names the fail-closed AC (AC2), and 'gate is in make lint' names the gate AC (AC6) plus its wiring AC (AC7).
evidence: DoD: "AC 4's enforcement test passes and fails correctly when the sandbox is disabled."
DoD: "AC 5's gate is in make lint with a covering test."
AC4 text is the portability criterion ('Portable per project.portability'); AC5 is 'The sandbox demonstrably DENIES'; AC6 is 'A lint gate flags...'; AC7 is 'That gate runs in make lint'.
findings.finding: The Definition of Done references acceptance criteria by number that do not match the Acceptance Criteria list's numbering: 'AC 4's enforcement test' points to the portability AC (AC4), while the enforcement/deny test is AC5 (and fail-closed is AC2); 'AC 5's gate is in make lint' points to the enforcement AC, while the lint gate is AC6 and its wiring into make lint is AC7.
findings.location: Definition of Done vs Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: An implementer following the DoD checks the wrong AC when confirming done-ness.
findings.suggested_fix: Renumber the DoD references: 'AC 5's enforcement test passes and AC 2's fail-closed abort fires when the sandbox is disabled'; 'AC 6's gate is in make lint (AC 7) with a covering test'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the Windows/BSD story for the sandbox: either name an OS facility for those platforms or explicitly document that on non-macOS/Linux hosts the gate requires the opt-out (accepting the unsandboxed risk there).
evidence: AC4: 'the mechanism is an OS facility (macOS Seatbelt sandbox-exec; a Linux equivalent such as bwrap/unshare)'
AC2: 'with no sandbox mechanism available the run ABORTS with an actionable message naming the opt-out'
Support matrix Platform cell includes Windows and BSD developer workstations; sandbox-exec and bwrap/unshare are absent there
findings.finding: AC4 names only macOS Seatbelt (sandbox-exec) and a Linux equivalent (bwrap/unshare) as the OS sandbox facility, but the support matrix also includes Windows and BSD workstations; on those platforms neither mechanism exists, so combined with the fail-closed AC2 the mutation gate ABORTS unless the operator sets the documented opt-out.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC4 ('macOS Seatbelt sandbox-exec; a Linux equivalent such as bwrap/unshare') and AC2 (fail-closed abort)
scenarios: A developer on a Windows workstation runs the mutation gate: no sandbox-exec or bwrap present, AC2 fires and the run aborts, so the mutation gate is unusable there unless the opt-out env var is set — leaving that platform unsandboxed by the only available path.
A developer on BSD hits the same abort with no documented sandbox mechanism named for that OS.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Commit to a specific Linux mechanism and verify (probe on a dev-host Linux) that it is available and actually denies out-of-allow-list writes without root/CI privileges — or name the availability precondition (unprivileged user namespaces / setuid) and the abort path when it is absent.
evidence: AC4: “a Linux equivalent such as `bwrap`/`unshare`” and “Verified by running `make lint` and the sandbox test on a developer host with no CI involved”
docs/mutation-testing.md:84 “Current mutation evidence is therefore Ubuntu-only; Windows and macOS portability is not established.”
No repo usage of `bwrap` — new external integration
Evidence class: Partially-verified — the facilities exist but neither their availability nor write-deny enforcement in the target dev environments is confirmed
findings.finding: The Linux mechanism is named only as an unresolved alternative (“`bwrap`/`unshare`”, “such as”) with no committed choice and no verification that it is available or enforces write-denial. `bwrap` and `unshare --map-root-user` both depend on unprivileged user namespaces (or setuid), which are disabled by default on some hardened distros — yet AC4 mandates verification “on a developer host with no CI involved,” i.e. on real dev laptops, a broader environment than the Ubuntu-only CI runner the existing mutation evidence covers.
scenarios: A contributor on a distro with unprivileged user namespaces disabled runs the mutation gate; `bwrap`/`unshare` fails to start and (per the fail-closed AC) aborts every mutation run, or the chosen mechanism silently lacks write-enforcement

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the OS sandbox and the destructive-test-exec lint gate belong in one ticket, or split the lint gate into its own child since each is independently valuable and releasable.
evidence: Scope 1: 'Sandbox the mutation run — the load-bearing control.'
Scope 2: 'A durable guard against destructive test-exec … a lint gate in the existing scripts/check_*.py family'
Two separate test files (test_mutation_sandbox.py, test_check_destructive_test_exec.py) and two separate deliverables (new sandbox module vs check script)
findings.finding: The ticket bundles two independently-releasable outcomes with different mechanisms and test files — an OS-enforced subprocess sandbox module and a static lint gate (check_destructive_test_exec.py) — which could each ship and be validated on their own.
scenarios: The sandbox module could land and be verified without the lint gate, and vice versa; keeping them coupled forces both through one review even though each is independently valuable defense-in-depth.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the default Linux sandbox mechanism (e.g. prefer bwrap, fall back to unshare --map-root-user) rather than leaving 'such as' open to the executor.
evidence: AC4: "the mechanism is an OS facility (macOS Seatbelt sandbox-exec; a Linux equivalent such as bwrap/unshare)"
findings.finding: The Linux sandbox mechanism is left as a choice for the executor ('a Linux equivalent such as bwrap/unshare') rather than a stated default, deferring a real design decision.
scenarios: The developer host is Linux and the executor must pick between bwrap and unshare, with different availability/privilege semantics (bwrap may need setuid; unshare needs user-namespace support).
findings.suggested_fix: Name the primary Linux mechanism and its fallback, and specify the availability probe order the fail-closed check (AC2) uses.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify (against a current macOS `man sandbox-exec` / a live probe) that `sandbox-exec` still enforces a write-deny profile on the target macOS versions, and record its deprecation status plus a fallback if Apple removes it — classify the evidence Verified, not Unverified.
evidence: AC4: “the mechanism is an OS facility (macOS Seatbelt `sandbox-exec`; a Linux equivalent such as `bwrap`/`unshare`)”
No repo usage of `sandbox-exec` — new external integration (only prior plan-review cache mentions it)
Evidence class: Unverified — `sandbox-exec` deprecation status and current enforcement behavior not confirmable from plan text or repo
findings.finding: The macOS control `sandbox-exec` (Seatbelt) is asserted as the load-bearing sandbox mechanism, but `sandbox-exec` is a deprecated Apple facility (its man page has carried a deprecation notice for years) and the plan neither acknowledges the deprecation nor verifies it still enforces filesystem-write denial on the target macOS versions. This is an asserted-but-unverified external capability the plan depends on.
scenarios: Author builds the wrapper on `sandbox-exec`; a future macOS removes it or the deprecated profile grammar changes, and the load-bearing control silently no-ops or errors

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how check_destructive_test_exec.py's scope (a Python test subprocess-execing a destructive shell script, seamed via RM_CMD) differs from the already-wired check_shellcheck.py SC2115 gate that catches the incident's `rm -rf "$var"/*` line, so the new gate covers the uncovered test-exec shape rather than re-catching the .sh-level defect.
evidence: scripts/check_shellcheck.py docstring: 'The motivating defect is **SC2115** … rm -rf "${dir}"/* … A gate configured at -S error would run green over the exact line that expanded to rm -rf /* on a contributor workstation and destroyed /opt/homebrew and /Applications.'
Makefile lines 260-263 already wire `python scripts/check_shellcheck.py` into `make lint`, describing SC2115 as catching 'the one that wiped /opt/homebrew and /Applications'.

The offending artifact named in the plan (mcp-entrypoint.sh) is a .sh file, which check_shellcheck.py's discover() (rglob('*.sh')) already scans — so the script-side of the incident is already covered.

The new gate's stated target IS distinct (a Python test that subprocess-execs a destructive shell script, seamed via RM_CMD), which SC2115 does not lint — so it is not a pure rebuild, but the delta is unstated.
findings.finding: The proposed check_destructive_test_exec.py lint gate overlaps with the existing, already-wired check_shellcheck.py (SC2115) gate without the plan acknowledging or delimiting that overlap.
scenarios: A reviewer or implementer questions whether AC6's gate duplicates the SC2115 coverage already green in make lint, since both cite the same rm -rf incident.
The new gate is built to re-catch a .sh-level defect that SC2115 already flags, wasting scope, instead of the distinct test-exec shape.
findings.suggested_fix: In Scope item 2 / AC6, add one sentence noting that SC2115 (via check_shellcheck.py, already in make lint) covers the destructive .sh line itself, and that this gate covers the orthogonal, uncovered case — a test that subprocess-execs such a script without an injectable seam — so the two are complementary, not duplicative.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Route a short SPIKE that proves deny-outside / permit-inside write enforcement for the chosen macOS and Linux facilities on real dev hosts before committing the full wrapper implementation.
evidence: Scope: “Sandbox the mutation run — the load-bearing control.”
AC5 requires observing enforcement but is validated post-implementation, not as an up-front feasibility gate
Incident-driven, security-critical control depending on two unverified external facilities
findings.finding: The plan commits to building the sandbox wrapper as the load-bearing, security-critical control without first routing a SPIKE to prove that either named OS facility actually enforces filesystem-write denial (deny-outside / permit-inside) in both target dev environments. AC5 asserts enforcement must be observed, but that test executes only after the mechanism is chosen and implemented; it does not de-risk the mechanism choice before the full plan is committed.
findings.location: Scope §1 (“Sandbox the mutation run — the load-bearing control”) / Acceptance Criteria AC5
scenarios: Full plan is implemented against `sandbox-exec`/`bwrap`; enforcement proves unavailable or non-enforcing on a target host late in the work, forcing a mechanism rework of the load-bearing control
